clue.text: Government employees making cars go

parts.note: Minis are small British cars, here in the plural
to have a go is to try, so go means try

explanation.surface: Civil servants are put to work producing motor vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a government department, the body of officials who staff it.

clue.text: A meditative expression, standing over piano offering gin

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second, so it stands over it

parts.note: a mantra is a word or phrase repeated in meditation
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone chanting in meditation sits at a piano while serving a gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare or trap, so a device for catching people fits.

clue.text: What could cover Adam's apple? Pet duck, perhaps

parts.note: to pet amorously is to neck
duck is a strong cotton or linen fabric, a kind of cloth

explanation.surface: A riddle about what might wrap a throat, answered with a pet duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks duck as one example of a fabric. Adam's apple is the bump at the front of the throat, so a cloth over it is worn at the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckcloth is a cravat worn round the throat, where the Adam's apple is.

clue.text: Cleaner more certain to get hold of business

indicators.note: the first word takes the business inside itself, holding it

parts.note: surer means more certain
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A cleaner, more sure of herself, lands some business.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad or person that cleans by scrubbing.

clue.text: Metal humidor has been revamped

indicators.note: revamped means remodelled, so the letters of humidor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cigar box has been refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a hard silvery metallic element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Greyish pink bit of chicken meat

definitions.meaning: a pale greyish-pink colour named after the shellfish
the small tender piece of dark meat on each side of a chicken's back

explanation.surface: Describing the colour of a scrap of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a greyish-pink shade and the choice morsel near a fowl's backbone.

clue.text: Attack directed at display of levity in the street

parts.note: on can mean directed at, as in an attack on someone

indicators.note: the display of levity is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a laugh shows light-heartedness

explanation.surface: An assault on someone who was laughing out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack.

clue.text: Japanese warlord in possession of head of thermonuclear weapon

indicators.note: the warlord holds the next letter inside him, possessing it

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Japanese military ruler acquires a nuclear warhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Circulatory problem makes windy character lose head and get doctor in

indicators.note: the doctor is put inside what remains of the wind god's name
the windy character drops his first letter

parts.note: Aeolus is the Greek god of the winds
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medical case where a flatulent man collapses and a doctor is called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' suggests flatulence, but the windy character is the god of the winds; 'lose head' drops his first letter, leaving EOLUS, and 'in' puts MB within that.
explanation.definitionFit: An embolus is a clot or air bubble blocking a blood vessel, a disorder of circulation.

clue.text: Corpse lion dug up in burial site

indicators.note: digging up disturbs things, so the letters of corpse and lion are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corpse and a lion are exhumed from a graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large ancient cemetery.

clue.text: Eyes son and brother from the back

indicators.note: the son and brother are read starting at the end

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a son and brother as they walk away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the back' turns the whole run SBRO around.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs is a poetic word for eyes.

clue.text: On tape, an investor who notes your every move

parts.note: something on tape is a recording
an angel is a backer of a theatrical production

explanation.surface: An investor is caught on tape as a watcher records everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The recording angel is the heavenly being said to write down every person's deeds.

clue.text: Here are the instructions — give a penny for first bit of coarse fabric

indicators.note: give here means put in, supplying the penny as a replacement letter
the penny takes the place of the opening letter of the fabric, standing for it

parts.note: grogram is a coarse fabric of silk and mohair
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An instruction sheet says to pay a penny for a scrap of rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'give a penny for' sounds like paying; here the penny symbol P replaces the G that starts GROGRAM. PROGRAM is the US and computing spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A program, in computing, is a set of instructions for a machine.

clue.text: Administrative centre busy early with reorganisation

indicators.note: reorganising puts things in a new order, so busy and early are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office is busy early in the day during a restructure.
explanation.walkthrough: AYLESBURY is the county town of Buckinghamshire, a county north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A county town is where a county's administration is based.

clue.text: Silver is stored in a particular rack

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the word is is kept inside the next piece

parts.note: one can mean a particular one, as in one day

explanation.surface: Silver is kept in a specific storage rack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rack oneself is to torment or agonise.

clue.text: Reprise — it takes a long time getting it up and running

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue reading up means the word it is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A rerun takes ages to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repetition, which an iteration also is.

clue.text: Will's hero returning to a welcome

indicators.note: the word to comes back, so its letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before turning
hello is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean hero comes home to a warm greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is William Shakespeare, whose Moorish general is the title character of a tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moor of Venice is the tragic hero of one of Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Habitual drinker has drunk up a small quantity

indicators.note: in a down clue the drunk is written upwards, so his letters run backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a spot is a small amount, as in a spot of lunch

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker has downed a little drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a drunkard.

clue.text: Blow up embattled general

indicators.note: an embattled general is in turmoil, so the letters of general are rearranged

explanation.surface: An embattled general is told to blow up the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to enlarge it.

clue.text: A cubic metre — very large but sound equipment

parts.note: a stere is a unit of volume equal to one cubic metre
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A massive cubic-metre box turns out to hold hi-fi gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereos are sound systems with two-channel playback.

clue.text: Bizarre mistake, going from city to country in the wrong direction

indicators.note: the whole run from city to country is read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to err is to make a mistake
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A navigational blunder takes a traveller from city to country the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going from city to country' fixes the order of the pieces; 'in the wrong direction' then turns the whole run around, giving LAERRUS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and strange, bizarre.

clue.text: Authorise raising military force to hold prisoner

indicators.note: the turned force holds the prisoner inside it
in a down clue raising means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A request to authorise mustering troops to guard a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British Army corps; 'raising' turns it to EMER in this down clue, and 'to hold' puts the captive inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority to act.

clue.text: Fault the church? Its teaching is straightforward

parts.note: a sin is a moral fault
CE is the Church of England
RE is religious education, the church's subject in schools

explanation.surface: A critic finds fault with the church but admits its teaching is honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is frank and genuine, straightforward.

clue.text: PM adopts scheme covering one military training area

parts.note: Lord Salisbury was a Victorian British prime minister

indicators.note: the scheme surrounds the one, covering it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prime minister backs a plan for an army exercise ground.
explanation.walkthrough: SALISBURY PLAIN is a chalk plateau in Wiltshire, southern England, used by the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The plateau in Wiltshire is the British Army's largest training ground.

clue.text: Length of wood used in box

definitions.meaning: a stout pole such as a mast or boom on a ship
to box is to fight with the fists, as boxers do in practice

explanation.surface: A piece of timber is used in a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a ship's pole and a verb for practice boxing.

clue.text: Accept liability for intruder we injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged, so the letters of intruder and we are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insurer takes responsibility for a burglar who hurt us.
explanation.definitionFit: To underwrite is to guarantee, taking on financial liability for a risk.

clue.text: Cold fish imprisoned in pen

indicators.note: the fish is shut inside the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cold fish is locked up in an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A steely manner is hard and cold.

clue.text: Palisade encircles my city

indicators.note: the fence goes round the exclamation, enclosing it

parts.note: a palisade is a fence of stakes
my and lor are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A fence is put around a person's city.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Italian city, capital of Tuscany.
